mainTopic: A נכרי in a shared courtyard: the גזירה behind the carrying ban, why a נכרי won't rent out his rights, and the ברייתא of רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
overview: The משנה taught that a Jew who shares a courtyard with a נכרי may not carry there unless he rents the נכרי's rights. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said this applies only when two Jews live there. The scholars first assume the argument is about whether a נכרי's home counts as a real דירה, but that leaves רבי אליעזר בן יעקב making no sense. אביי proves from a ברייתא that a נכרי's courtyard is like an animal pen, so everyone agrees it is not a real דירה. The real argument is about a rabbinic גזירה, made so that the Jew will not learn from the נכרי's ways. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב applies it only to the common case of two Jews, while רבי מאיר says even a lone Jew sometimes lives there. The גזירה works because a נכרי will not rent out his rights. The גמרא defines a full rental (with legal documents and officials) and a flawed one (without them). It explains that the נכרי fears losing his property under a full rental and fears כשפים under a token one. Finally, the גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes the full disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The scholars assume the dispute is about whether a non-Jew's home counts as a residence
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רב חיננא בר אבין, with אביי sitting next to them, propose that רבי מאיר holds a נכרי's home counts as a real דירה. If so, he forbids carrying whether one Jew or two live in the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: אביי בר אבין and רב חיננא בר אבין were sitting, and אביי was sitting beside them. They sat and said: We understand רבי מאיר. He holds that a נכרי's home is considered a real residence, so it makes no difference whether one Jew or two Jews live in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a scene of scholars discussing the משנה. They first explain רבי מאיר's view in a way that works smoothly, and this sets up a problem with the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars' starting idea is that the whole מחלוקת depends on one question: does a נכרי's home count as a דירה? If it does, the נכרי is a real resident who has a share in the courtyard. Since he cannot join an עירוב, he blocks carrying even for a single Jew, and that fits רבי מאיר exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: granted / it makes sense regarding (sets up a contrast with the next opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named אביי here. אביי בר אבין is one of the two brothers. The 'אביי' who sits beside them, and who answers in step 3, is the famous אביי.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chinana bar Avin were sitting,
and Abaye was sitting beside them,
phrases.notes: This is the famous אביי, not אביי בר אבין.

phrases.english: and they sat and said:
Granted, Rabbi Meir holds
that a non-Jew's residence is considered a residence,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא חַד וְלָא שְׁנָא תְּרֵי.
phrases.english: so there is no difference between one and two.
phrases.notes: One Jew or two Jews in the courtyard: either way, carrying is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about a Jew sharing a courtyard with a נכרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the proposed reading, רבי מאיר holds דירת גוי שמה דירה, so the נכרי forbids carrying whether one or two Jews live there.

steps.title: The opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב seems to make no sense
steps.stepSummary: Under that assumption, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view seems impossible. Either the נכרי's home is a דירה, so even one Jew should be forbidden, or it is not, so even two Jews should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב hold? If he holds that a נכרי's home counts as a residence, carrying should be forbidden even with one Jew! And if it does not count as a residence, carrying should not be forbidden even with two Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars challenge רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view. They show that the 'is it a residence or not' explanation cannot account for his middle position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב draws a line between one Jew and two Jews. But the question 'is a נכרי's home a דירה?' is a plain yes-or-no question, and it should give the same answer no matter how many Jews live there. So under this assumption his distinction has no basis, and that shows the assumption itself is shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: he should forbid / it should be forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is right. It is that, under the assumed framework, his view has no logic at all.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב מַאי קָסָבַר?
phrases.english: But Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, what does he hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר דִּירַת גּוֹי שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה —
phrases.english: If he holds that a non-Jew's residence is considered a residence —
he should forbid even with one as well!
And if it is not considered a residence —
he should not forbid even with two!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא structure. Step 1 explained רבי מאיר; this step shows the same framework fails for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the מחלוקת depends on whether דירת גוי שמה דירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A yes-or-no status of the נכרי's home cannot produce a distinction between one Jew and two Jews.

steps.title: אביי proves רבי מאיר does not consider a non-Jew's home a residence
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the whole starting assumption. He cites a ברייתא: a נכרי's courtyard is like an animal pen. So even רבי מאיר does not treat a נכרי's home as a real דירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Does רבי מאיר really hold that a נכרי's home counts as a residence? But it was taught in a ברייתא: a נכרי's courtyard is like an animal pen.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the basic premise of the discussion, using a ברייתא as evidence. He shows that the starting explanation of רבי מאיר is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal pen does not count as a residence for עירוב purposes, so it does not block anyone from carrying. If a נכרי's courtyard is 'like an animal pen', his home is not a real דירה. That knocks out the explanation from step 1, so the problem from step 2 never really started.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
like an animal pen (not a legal residence)

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר דִּירַת גּוֹי שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Meir hold that a non-Jew's residence is considered a residence?
But wasn't it taught:
The courtyard of a non-Jew —
it is like the pen of an animal.
phrases.notes: Just as an animal pen does not forbid carrying, neither does the non-Jew's home by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר דִּירַת גּוֹי שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of answering the difficulty in step 2, אביי removes the premise of step 1 on which it was built.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire framework that the מחלוקת is about whether דירת גוי שמה דירה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that a נכרי's courtyard is like an animal pen, so even רבי מאיר does not consider it a real דירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: חצירו של נכרי הרי הוא כדיר של בהמה.

steps.title: Everyone agrees it is not a residence; they argue about a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: אביי re-explains the מחלוקת. All agree a נכרי's home is not a real דירה. The restriction comes from a rabbinic גזירה made out of concern that the Jew might learn from the נכרי's ways. רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue only about when that גזירה applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that a נכרי's home is not considered a residence. Here they argue about a גזירה, made out of concern that the Jew might learn from the נכרי's ways.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new explanation of the whole argument in the משנה. It replaces the one he just rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly by law, the נכרי does not block carrying at all. The חכמים made a גזירה to make living alongside a נכרי unpleasant, so that the Jew would not move in with him and learn his ways. רבי מאיר applies the גזירה even to a single Jew. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב applies it only when two Jews live there, since a single Jew rarely moves in with a נכרי. This finally gives his one-versus-two line a clear reason.

keyTerms.meaning: lest he learn from his (the non-Jew's) ways

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי's home is not a real דירה according to anyone. The ban on carrying with a נכרי in the courtyard is a rabbinic גזירה, so that the Jew won't learn from his ways. רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argue only about whether that גזירה reaches a single Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reframes the whole category. The restriction is not about the נכרי's legal ownership of the courtyard. It is a protective rabbinic rule, and that is what lets its scope depend on practical factors like how many Jews live there.

phrases.english: Rather: everyone agrees
that a non-Jew's residence is not considered a residence,
and here, regarding a decree
lest he learn from his ways,
they disagree.
phrases.notes: The question is whether the decree applies to one Jew (רבי מאיר) or only to two (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא דִּירַת גּוֹי לֹא שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new framework after step 3 rejected the old one, and it resolves the problem raised in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת was thought to be about whether דירת גוי שמה דירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree it is not a דירה. The argument is about the reach of the גזירה שמא ילמד ממעשיו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prohibition is a rabbinic גזירה; its scope (one Jew or two) is what the תנאים dispute.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the decree covers only two Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that the גזירה applies only to two Jews living with a נכרי. Two Jews commonly do this, while one Jew alone rarely does, out of fear for his safety.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds: since a נכרי is suspected of murder, two Jews, who commonly live with him, were included in the decree. One Jew does not commonly live with him, so the Rabbis did not make the decree for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's answer and explains the reasoning of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The גזירה is aimed only at the common case of two Jews living with a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lone Jew would be afraid to live next to someone suspected of violence, so that case almost never happens. Two Jews protect each other, so they do live with a נכרי. The Rabbis only make decrees for common situations, so only the two-Jew case is included.
steps.confusionAlert: Remember the result is reversed from what you might expect. One Jew is allowed to carry and two Jews are forbidden. This is not because one Jew is more protected. It is only because the Rabbis did not bother decreeing about a rare case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds:
since a gentile is suspected of bloodshed,
two (Jews), who commonly live (with him) —
they decreed regarding them;
one (Jew) is not common —
phrases.notes: A lone Jew would be afraid to live alone with him.

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not decree regarding him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of אביי's answer from step 4 for the first side of the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the scope of a rabbinic decree based on how common the case is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-Jew versus one-Jew difference seemed to make no sense, because a נכרי's home either is a דירה or is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference comes from how common each case is. The status of the נכרי's home is not the issue.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: even one Jew sometimes lives there
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a single Jew does sometimes live with a נכרי, so the גזירה covers him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר holds: sometimes it happens that (one Jew) lives there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי מאיר's side of the מחלוקת, still as part of אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees with the basic idea of the גזירה. He disagrees only about the facts: a lone Jew living with a נכרי happens often enough to be included. So in his view the restriction applies whether there is one Jew or two.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir holds:
sometimes it happens that (even one Jew) lives (there).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual disagreement about how common a case is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר forbids one Jew because he treats a נכרי's home as a real דירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר forbids one Jew only because that case is common enough to be included in the גזירה.

steps.title: How the decree works: the gentile must rent, and he won't
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ruled that an עירוב and ביטול רשות do not work where a נכרי lives unless he rents out his rights. Since a נכרי will not rent, the Jew is stuck and will want to move.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis said: an עירוב does not work where a נכרי lives, and giving up rights (ביטול רשות) does not work where a נכרי lives, until he rents (out his rights). And a נכרי will not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the גזירה actually pushes Jews away from living with a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way to permit carrying is for the נכרי to rent out his rights in the courtyard. A נכרי usually refuses, so the Jew cannot carry on שבת. The discomfort encourages him to move away, which protects him from learning the נכרי's ways.

keyTerms.meaning: A shared food arrangement that lets neighbors carry in a common courtyard on שבת
Giving up one's rights in the courtyard to the other residents

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule behind the whole topic. A Jew sharing a courtyard with a נכרי needs a rental from him before an עירוב can work.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said:
an eiruv is not effective in a place (where) a gentile (lives),

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מוֹעִיל בִּמְקוֹם גּוֹי,
phrases.english: and renouncing rights is not effective in a place (where) a gentile (lives),
until he rents (out his rights).
And a gentile does not rent (them out).
phrases.notes: So the Jew will be uncomfortable and will move away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עֵירוּב מוֹעִיל בִּמְקוֹם גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the גזירה described in steps 4-6 works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where a נכרי lives, neither an עירוב nor ביטול רשות works unless he rents out his rights. He normally will not.

steps.title: Why won't the gentile rent? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a נכרי refuses to rent. It suggests he fears the Jews will take over his property, but notes this works only for the view that requires a real rental.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason (the נכרי won't rent)? If you say it is because he thinks they may come to take hold of his property, that works well for the one who says we need a real rental.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the last line, "a נכרי will not rent." It offers a possible answer and starts setting up a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rental must be a full, legally valid rental, the נכרי could worry that it gives the Jews real rights in his home. So his refusal makes sense under that view. The word הניחא ("this works well") signals that a difficulty for the other view is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: To take possession, to claim ownership
This works well (for one view, but not the other)
A real, full, legally valid rental

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because he thinks:
perhaps they will come to take possession of his property,
this works well according to the one who says:
we require a full-fledged rental.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind the statement in step 7 that a נכרי will not rent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a נכרי refuses to rent out his rights for an עירוב.

steps.title: The problem: a token rental should not scare him
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that only a token rental is needed, the נכרי has no reason to fear losing his property. So why would he refuse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says we need only a weak (token) rental, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggested reason from step 8. It does not work for the view that a symbolic rental is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A token rental gives the Jews no real rights, and the נכרי would understand that. Then fear of losing his property cannot explain why he refuses. So the suggested reason fails for this view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (signals a difficulty)

steps.confusionAlert: In this phrase רעועה does not mean an invalid rental that fails. It means a light, symbolic rental that is still good enough for עירוב purposes.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
we require (only) a flawed, token rental,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הניחא / אלא pattern by showing where the suggestion from step 8 breaks down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason that the נכרי refuses to rent out of fear of losing his property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a token rental is enough, nothing real is at stake, so the fear makes no sense.

steps.title: The source: רב חסדא and רב ששת's dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the dispute it just mentioned. רב חסדא requires a real rental, and רב ששת says a token rental is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: רב חסדא said a real rental (is needed), and רב ששת said a token rental (is enough).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two אמוראים behind the two views it just mentioned. This shows the difficulty from step 9 is based on a real opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase דאתמר introduces a documented dispute. רב ששת's view is the one that makes the question in step 9 serious. The גמרא first defines the two kinds of rental (steps 11-14), and then answers the question in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (introducing a dispute of אמוראים)
אמורא who requires a full rental
אמורא who accepts a token rental

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה pushes Jews away from living with a נכרי, because he will not rent out his rights. The next question is why he won't, especially according to רב ששת, who says even a token rental is enough. Step 16 answers this.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
Rav Chisda said: a full-fledged rental.
And Rav Sheshet said: a flawed, token rental.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the two opinions referred to in steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא requires a full rental from the נכרי, while רב ששת says a token rental is enough.

steps.title: What exactly is a flawed rental versus a full rental?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שכירות רעועה and שכירות בריאה mean. It suggests the difference is paying a פרוטה versus paying less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'flawed' rental, and what is a 'full' rental? If you say a full rental is for a פרוטה and a flawed rental is for less than a פרוטה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for definitions of the two kinds of rental mentioned in the dispute. It offers a first guess about the amount of money paid, and this guess sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא and רב ששת argued over whether the rental must be 'full' or can be 'flawed', but neither term has been defined yet. The first guess is that the difference is the price. A פרוטה is the smallest amount that normally counts as money in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)
The smallest coin that counts as money in הלכה
Less than the value of a פרוטה

phrases.english: What is 'flawed', what is 'full-fledged'?
If you say: full-fledged means for a peruta,
flawed means for less than the value of a peruta.
phrases.notes: This suggestion is about to be challenged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the two terms used in רב חסדא and רב ששת's dispute in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between a flawed rental and a full-fledged rental.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First guess: a full rental costs a פרוטה, and a flawed rental costs less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: From a נכרי, even less than a פרוטה works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first guess. רבי יוחנן taught that one may rent from a נכרי even for less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anyone who says that renting from a נכרי for less than a פרוטה does not work? But רבי יצחק son of רבי יעקב בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: Know that we may rent from a נכרי even for less than a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first guess. Nobody holds that less than a פרוטה fails to work for a rental from a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a flawed rental meant 'less than a פרוטה', then רב חסדא would hold that such a rental does not work. But רבי יוחנן ruled that renting from a נכרי for less than a פרוטה is fine, and no one disagrees. So the dispute cannot be about the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone who says...? (meaning: no one says that)
Sent (a ruling sent by letter, often from ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Is there anyone who says
that from a gentile, for less than a peruta, it does not work?
But Rabbi Yitzchak sent
son of Rabbi Yaakov bar Giyorei
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Be aware that we rent from a gentile
even for less than the value of a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִגּוֹי בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first definition offered in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition that a flawed rental means paying less than a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that definition, רב חסדא would invalidate renting for less than a פרוטה. But רבי יוחנן says it is valid from a נכרי, and no one argues.

steps.title: For a נכרי, less than a פרוטה still counts as money
steps.stepSummary: A second ruling of רבי יוחנן shows why: a בן נח is killed for stealing even less than a פרוטה. So for a נכרי, a tiny amount is real money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A בן נח is executed for stealing less than a פרוטה, and returning it does not fix the sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that backs up the challenge. It shows that, in the world of a נכרי, even less than a פרוטה counts as real value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that 'less than a פרוטה is not money' applies only to Jews. A נכרי cares about even tiny amounts, so stealing a tiny amount is a capital crime for a בן נח. So a tiny payment to a נכרי is a real payment, and a rental for it works.

keyTerms.meaning: A descendant of Noach, a non-Jew bound by the seven Noahide laws
To be returned (fixing a theft by giving back the item)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג עַל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה,
phrases.english: A Noahide is executed for stealing less than a peruta,
and it was not given to be fixed by returning it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of Step 12 by giving the reason behind it.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that for a נכרי, less than a פרוטה counts as money, so renting for it works.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a בן נח is executed for stealing less than a פרוטה.
steps.confusionAlert: This ruling is not about rentals. It is brought only to show that for a נכרי, a tiny amount counts as real money.

steps.title: New definition: legal documents and officials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new definition. A full rental is backed by legal documents and officials. A flawed rental is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a full rental is one made with legal documents and officials. A flawed rental is one made without legal documents and officials.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first guess failed, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question of Step 11. The difference is how official the rental is, not how much is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full rental is legally binding, with documents and officials who can enforce it. A flawed rental is an informal deal that a court would not enforce. This explains why a נכרי might fear a full rental: it gives the Jews real legal rights in his property.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
Officials who guarantee or enforce the deal

phrases.english: Rather: full-fledged means with legal documents and officials,
flawed means without legal documents and officials.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the definition from Step 11 that was rejected in Steps 12-13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The difference between a flawed and a full rental (from Step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A full rental is legally binding with documents and officials. A flawed rental lacks them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This definition sets up the next step. It explains why a נכרי would fear a full rental, but it does not yet explain why he would refuse a token one. Step 16 answers that.

steps.title: The question returns: why refuse even a token rental?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the terms are defined, the גמרא repeats its earlier challenge. Under רב חסדא it is clear why a נכרי refuses, but under רב ששת, why would he refuse an informal rental?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says we need a full rental. But for the one who says a flawed rental is enough, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from Steps 8-9, now using the new definition. It shows the difficulty only exists for the view that a token rental is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rental must be legally binding, a נכרי fears the Jews could use it to take over his property, so he refuses. But a token rental with no documents gives the Jews no legal hold. So under רב ששת the reason for his refusal is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (asks for an answer for the other view)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says:
we require a full-fledged rental.
But for the one who says:
we require only a flawed rental,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: שְׂכִירוּת בְּרִיאָה בָּעִינַן. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definition from Step 14 to restate the challenge first raised in Steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (Step 7) that a נכרי will not rent out his rights, under רב ששת's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A token rental without documents gives the Jews no legal hold, so a נכרי has no reason to fear it and should agree.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question from Steps 8-9, repeated now that we know what 'full' and 'flawed' mean.

steps.title: The נכרי fears witchcraft
steps.stepSummary: Even with a token rental, the נכרי suspects the Jews are casting a spell on him, so he refuses to rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the נכרי worries about witchcraft, and he does not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The נכרי's fear is not about losing property but about כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב ששת, the נכרי has nothing to lose legally. But he sees Jews wanting to 'rent' his rights in an odd way and suspects it is a magic ritual against him. So he refuses either way, and the Jew is still stuck, as Step 7 said.

phrases.english: Even so, the gentile worries about witchcraft,
and he does not rent out.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the same behavior: fear of כשפים instead of fear of losing property.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a property fear, a נכרי would gladly agree to a token rental.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נכרי refuses even a token rental because he fears it is witchcraft, so under both views he does not rent.
steps.whatToRemember: Full rental = with legal documents and officials. Flawed rental = without them (not about paying a פרוטה, since from a נכרי even less than a פרוטה counts). A נכרי refuses a full rental because he fears losing his property, and a token rental because he fears כשפים. Either way the Jew cannot make an עירוב and will want to move.

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא: A Gentile's Courtyard Is Like an Animal Pen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it quoted earlier. A courtyard with only a נכרי's houses is treated like an animal pen, so carrying between the houses and the courtyard is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main text: A נכרי's courtyard is like an animal pen. It is allowed to carry things in and out, from the courtyard to the houses and from the houses to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to the ברייתא it mentioned during the earlier discussion, so it can study it line by line. The first line says a courtyard of only a נכרי has no carrying problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of עירובי חצרות only apply to Jewish homes. A נכרי's house does not count as a 'residence' for these laws, just like a pen where animals live. So nothing in the courtyard needs an עירוב, and carrying between the houses and the courtyard is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא is returning to a source it quoted earlier so it can study it directly.
An animal pen. It is a place where creatures live, but it is not a 'home' for the laws of עירוב.
To carry in and to carry out between one area and another.
A courtyard shared by several houses.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the נכרי is compared to an animal as a person. The comparison is only about the laws of עירוב: his house, like a pen, is not counted as a residence that needs to join in an עירוב.

phrases.english: The matter itself: The courtyard of a gentile
phrases.notes: גופא means the גמרא is going back to look more closely at the ברייתא it quoted earlier.

phrases.english: is like the pen of an animal,
and it is permitted to carry in and to carry out
from the courtyard to the houses
and from the houses to the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: חֲצֵירוֹ שֶׁל גּוֹי הֲרֵי הוּא כְּדִיר שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion about renting from a נכרי ends here. The גמרא now studies the ברייתא that was quoted during that discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A courtyard with only a נכרי's houses is like an animal pen, and carrying between the houses and the courtyard is permitted.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Even One Jew Living There Is Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that if even one Jew lives in the courtyard with the נכרי, the נכרי forbids that Jew to carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one Jew lives there, the נכרי forbids carrying. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי מאיר says that once even a single Jew lives in the courtyard, the נכרי's presence forbids that Jew from carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no Jew there, the courtyard had no problem. Adding just one Jew changes the result according to רבי מאיר. The Jew may not carry between his house and the courtyard unless he rents the נכרי's rights, which ties back to the earlier discussion of renting. The reason was already given in steps 4 and 6: a rabbinic גזירה, so that the Jew won't learn from the נכרי's ways, and a lone Jew sometimes does live with a נכרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbids. Here it means the נכרי makes it forbidden for the Jew to carry.
'The words of רבי מאיר.' This marks the opinion as his, and a disagreement usually follows.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opinion that makes renting from a נכרי necessary even for a lone Jew. That is the background for the whole earlier rental discussion.

phrases.english: But if there is one Jew there —
he (the gentile) prohibits; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: The subject of אוסר is the נכרי, who forbids the Jew to carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶחָד — אוֹסֵר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This adds a case to the first rule. A courtyard with only a נכרי is fine, but once one Jew lives there, carrying becomes forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a נכרי forbids carrying in the courtyard even when only one Jew lives there with him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: Only When Two Jews Live There
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with רבי מאיר. The נכרי forbids carrying only when there are two Jews who would already forbid each other without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The נכרי never forbids carrying unless there are two Jews who would forbid each other.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with רבי מאיר. He says one Jew alone with a נכרי may carry freely. The problem starts only when there are two Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single Jew alone in a courtyard never needs an עירוב, because there is no one to join with. When two Jews share the courtyard, they need an עירוב, and the נכרי's presence blocks it from working. The deeper reason was given in step 5: the גזירה was made only for the common case of two Jews, since a lone Jew rarely lives with a נכרי.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with רבי מאיר here.
'Always' or 'never.' Here it means the נכרי never forbids, except in the case that follows.
Until there are, meaning 'unless there are.'
Forbid one another. Two Jews in one courtyard need an עירוב in order to carry.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions on a נכרי in a shared courtyard. רבי מאיר says even one Jew is forbidden to carry. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the נכרי forbids only when there are two Jews who would need an עירוב with each other anyway.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
Actually, he (the gentile) does not prohibit
unless there are two Jews
who prohibit one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposing view to רבי מאיר in step 18, within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a נכרי forbids carrying only when two Jews share the courtyard and would otherwise need an עירוב with each other.
